# Activation Evidence

Form the initial explanation from `/inputs/report/index.html` and its structured measurement files. This container performs the first stage only.

Read the report by section with scripts/read_evidence.py. For HTML layout, read the markup around the section you need. The self-contained HTML and measurement JSON also embed millions of numeric values; load those files in Python and select named fields or cases instead of printing whole files into the conversation. All evidence remains available through the section and case queries.

## Read the focused references

- [API reference](references/api-reference.md): sections, sample groups and pagination.
- [Workflows](references/workflows.md): commands for statistics and natural contexts.

## Read the measurements

The target report is mounted read-only at `/inputs/report`. Run the bundled `scripts/read_evidence.py` to list evidence from that same report. Fetch the sections and contexts needed for the explanation. Positive and negative extremes show the strongest responses; weaker quantile cases help establish the scope of the pattern.

Explain product activation. A measured positive product is the positive response pole; a measured negative product is the negative response pole. The tools determine this sign. Semantic group descriptions are provisional interpretations of context and do not change it. Compare the positive and negative members, their magnitudes and prefixes before adopting a directional explanation. Small nonzero values have a sign but give weak evidence for an association. Revise broad definitions contradicted by recurring strong responses. Gate and value support that explanation. Read each observed prefix together with its measured anchor. Following text is a prediction target. Token selectivity thresholds are fractions of the signed corpus extreme, not percentiles.

## Submit the initial explanation

Alongside the claim, submit response_rules: a compact list of textual conditions that predict positive, negative or uncertain product responses at a specified token. Use roughly six to eight rules when supported. Each rule contains id, name, description and predicted_pole. Explain the triggering context and position, including boundary cases; do not define a rule by the measured sign alone. These rules state the current explanation and are frozen when you submit.

Send the claim through `scripts/submit_interpretation.py`; see the [workflow](references/workflows.md). The tool saves the initial explanation and returns its report path. Stop after it returns.

## Writing

Write a short title in the form “[concept] neuron”, with an optional phrase describing its response. Begin the explanation directly with what this neuron responds to or changes. Refer to the measured unit as “this neuron”; keep its layer and index in the identification fields.

Use ordinary descriptions of the positive and negative responses. Describe sparsity in the activation-distribution discussion, rather than calling the neuron a “sparse feature”. Keep qualifications in sentences instead of stacking them in a long title.

Describe the observations and conclusions directly for the reader.

Use approximate English word targets: lede 60–85; one_paragraph 150–180; negative_pole 80–120; what_would_change_my_mind 40–60. The latter three fields are the three paragraphs of The claim in detail. State the main pattern, a few decisive measurements and the material limitation; keep exhaustive statistics and sample-by-sample discussion in evidence. These are writing targets, not output limits.

# Evidence API

Run `scripts/read_evidence.py` relative to this skill directory. With no arguments it returns the evidence index for the assigned neuron. The host reads the target-only report package mounted at `/inputs/report`; the full activation archive and other neurons are not mounted.

Options:

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--section` | `index`, `distribution`, `contexts`, `token_selectivity`, `peak_census`, `gate_value`, `output_effects`, or `all` |
| `--group` | One context group listed by the index |
| `--ids` | Specific case IDs |
| `--offset` | First context in the filtered list; default 0 |
| `--limit` | Contexts per page; default 4 |

A context page returns `total`, `offset`, `next_offset`, `trace_columns` and `cases`. Pagination retains the full observed prefix, anchor, local gate/value/product trace and following prediction target. It does not shorten a context.


The six token selectivity tables use Top20 rows and occurrence count at least 50. Thresholds are fractions of the signed corpus maximum/minimum. Positive, negative and absolute peak censuses are separate. The gate_value response supplies numeric rows at data.scatter, ordered by data.scatter_columns (gate, value, product). In raw report.json, scatter is a list of case IDs; their numeric rows are points[case_id].values. Output effects contain the existing static projections and native ablations.

Claim prose uses approximate English word targets: lede 60–85, one_paragraph 150–180, negative_pole 80–120, what_would_change_my_mind 40–60. The latter three fields appear as the three paragraphs of The claim in detail; supporting evidence remains available separately.

Submit response_rules alongside claim. Each rule has id, name, description and predicted_pole (`positive`, `negative` or `uncertain`). The description states the textual conditions and anchor location under which that prediction follows from the claim.

# Evidence workflows

Run these commands from this skill directory.

```bash
python scripts/read_evidence.py
python scripts/read_evidence.py --section distribution
python scripts/read_evidence.py --section token_selectivity
python scripts/read_evidence.py --section peak_census
python scripts/read_evidence.py --section gate_value
python scripts/read_evidence.py --section output_effects
python scripts/read_evidence.py --section contexts --offset 0 --limit 4
```

Read further contexts at `next_offset`, filter by a group returned by the index, or request specific IDs:

```bash
python scripts/read_evidence.py --section contexts --group top_tokens --limit 4
python scripts/read_evidence.py --section contexts --ids CASE_ID
```

Base the explanation on the supplied activation evidence. The evidence tool returns saved measurements.

## Submit this stage

```bash
python scripts/submit_interpretation.py <<'JSON'
{"claim":{"title":"","lede":"","one_paragraph":"","negative_pole":"","what_would_change_my_mind":"","confidence":""},"criticism":[],"response_rules":[{"id":"rule_1","name":"Short contextual condition","description":"State the observed textual condition and anchor position that imply this response.","predicted_pole":"positive"}]}
JSON
```

Fill the claim from the saved evidence. Detailed experimental Criticism is written in stage three. The script saves the initial explanation and an HTML copy; stop when it returns.
